name: Google NotebookLM
description: Source-grounded AI research workspace built on Gemini. A notebook is a bounded corpus of user-uploaded sources (PDF, web, video, EPUB, images, CSV) plus a chat grounded strictly in those sources and generated artifacts (summaries, Audio/Video Overviews, mind maps, slide decks, quizzes). The workspace boundary is a curated source set rather than a filesystem directory.
user_identity_model: Required Google account authentication (consumer Google account, or Google Workspace / Workspace for Education account for the managed tiers). NotebookLM Enterprise (delivered via Google Cloud / Gemini Enterprise / Agentspace) authenticates through organizational identity: Cloud Identity (Google IdP) or Workforce Identity Federation (e.g., Okta). There is no device-local / no-account mode and no API-key path for end users; identity is mandatory and tied to a Google identity. Tier determines TOS scope: Google TOS for personal accounts, Google Workspace TOS for work accounts, Workspace for Education TOS for education accounts.
multi_user_collaboration: Supported on paid/managed tiers. NotebookLM Plus and Enterprise allow shared notebooks: the owner shares a notebook by email invite (comma-separated addresses) or shareable link, with two permission levels. Viewer can interact/query but cannot upload sources or add notes; Editor has owner-equivalent rights except cannot delete, share, or revoke access. Highest permission wins when a user is in multiple groups. Enterprise restricts sharing to users in the same Google Cloud project, same workforce pool, holding the Cloud NotebookLM User role and a NotebookLM/Gemini Enterprise license. Org-level data trust boundary: uploads, queries, and responses stay within the organization's boundary and are not used for training. Concurrent access is supported; saved notes/sources/generated artifacts are visible to all collaborators, but each user's chat history remains private to that user.
workspace_definition: A 'workspace' is a notebook: an abstract, account-scoped entity stored in Google's cloud, defined by its bounded curated source set (not a directory or git repo, and fully virtual). Each notebook holds up to 50 sources on Free (100 Plus / 300 Pro / 600 Ultra), each source up to 500,000 words or 200MB. Users can hold up to 100 notebooks on Free (up to ~500 on Pro). The notebook is the unit of grounding, sharing, generated artifacts (Audio/Video Overview, mind map, slide deck, infographic, data table, quiz, flashcards), and chat scope. This is a strong example of workspace = curated corpus scope rather than workspace = filesystem path.
workspace_session_binding: Chat is scoped per-notebook. As of late 2025 (100% rollout by Dec 17, 2025), each notebook persists its own conversation record so a user can close and resume a chat within that notebook. Chat history is per-user-per-notebook and private to the user even on shared notebooks. There is no single cross-notebook conversation view and no documented support for multiple distinct concurrent named chat sessions within one notebook (the model is one resumable running chat thread per notebook per user, with the ability to clear it). Sessions are bound to the notebook (workspace), not to the user globally. [uncertain]
context_scoping: Context is almost entirely notebook-scoped: the source corpus, generated artifacts, saved notes, and chat are all bound to a single notebook and do not bleed across notebooks. Retrieval is constrained to the active notebook's sources (closed RAG). A customizable goal/persona and the 1M-token Gemini context window apply within the notebook's chat. There is no global cross-notebook memory or instruction layer inside NotebookLM itself; cross-notebook reach is only achieved externally by mounting notebooks as data sources in the Gemini App (early 2026). No per-directory or nested config concept exists.
config_file_instruction_precedence: Not applicable in the file/cascade sense. NotebookLM has no config files (no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md analog), no directory cascade, and no file-size cap on instructions. Behavior is shaped only through UI affordances: per-notebook chat goal/persona/customization settings and the selection of which sources are active for a given query. Instruction scope is effectively per-notebook only. [uncertain]
source_corpus_grounding_scope: Core design. The notebook is defined by a bounded source set and all answers are grounded strictly in those sources via closed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over Gemini (Gemini 2.5 Flash class). Supported source types: PDF, Google Docs/Slides, pasted text, web URLs, YouTube/video, audio, EPUB (early 2026), images with OCR, and CSV. Sources are added via upload (≤200MB or ≤500,000 words each) or link. Retrieval is constrained to the active notebook's sources, with inline clickable citations pointing to the exact source passage; if no relevant passage is found, the model is designed to say so rather than invent. Users can narrow retrieval by selecting/deselecting specific sources. Reported response-level hallucination rate ~13% vs ~40% for ungrounded LLMs. Very large single sources may only be partially scanned, so splitting documents is advised.
persistence_mechanism: Cloud-only, managed by Google. On upload, NotebookLM creates a secure static analytical snapshot/copy of each source stored on Google infrastructure; the model never reads the user's live document. Notebooks, sources, notes (up to 1,000 per notebook), generated artifacts, and (since late 2025) per-user chat history are persisted server-side. Storage is mutable from the user's perspective (edit/add/remove sources and notes) and terminal: deleting a notebook or removing a source hard-deletes the associated snapshot, research, and conversation history with no native recovery. Underlying datastore is not publicly documented (Google Cloud internal infrastructure; Enterprise builds on Google Cloud / Agentspace data stores). [uncertain]
session_history: Chat history is stored per-notebook, private per user, browsable in the chat panel, and resumable across sessions/devices (web and mobile). It is auto-saved. There is no cross-notebook history search, no published fixed retention window, and no dedicated native export of raw chat history. Users can manually persist individual answers via 'Save to note' (preserves tables and inline citations, but is view-only and excludes the user's prompt). Chat history can be cleared via the chat panel's three-dot 'Delete Chat History'. Internal storage format is not publicly documented. [uncertain]
memory_layering: Limited layering. Durable, user-authored/curated state lives as the notebook corpus plus saved notes (explicit user action). Ephemeral thread state is the resumable per-notebook chat (now auto-persisted but still per-notebook and not a cross-thread memory store). There is no auto-generated long-term cross-notebook memory analogous to Windsurf/Claude auto-memory, and no distinction between a global durable store and short-term state beyond 'sources/notes vs. chat thread.' Customizable goals/persona act as lightweight per-notebook standing instructions. [uncertain]
search_retrieval_history: No cross-notebook history search and no semantic search over past conversations. Chat history is per-notebook only with no single aggregated view. To carry information from one session to another within a notebook, the chat is auto-resumed; to carry it across notebooks, users must save answers as notes or externally mount notebooks into the Gemini App (early 2026 cross-notebook querying via Gemini, not native NotebookLM history search). Retrieval search at query time is semantic RAG over the active notebook's sources, not over conversation history.
lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Persistent by default rather than ephemeral: notebooks, sources, notes, and chat history persist until the user deletes them. No published TTL or auto-expiration for notebooks or chat history. Deletion is hard deletion with no native archive/recovery — removing a source or notebook permanently destroys its snapshot and associated chat/research. Daily usage caps exist (e.g., Free: 50 chat queries/day, 3 audio generations/day; Ultra up to ~5,000 chats and ~200 audio/day) but these are rate limits, not lifecycle/cleanup of stored state. [uncertain]
sandbox_isolation_model: Not a code-execution sandbox. Each notebook is an isolated logical data scope within Google's multi-tenant cloud; the closed RAG system ensures one notebook/user's sources are never retrievable by another user. There is no per-session VM/container, no git worktree, no user-controllable network policy, and no user code execution — 'isolation' here means corpus/data isolation and the static snapshot boundary (the AI works on a copy, never the live document). Enterprise adds organizational trust-boundary isolation (data stays within the org's Google Cloud project and is not used for training). Resource limits are expressed as tier quotas.
snapshot_state_restore: There is a one-way snapshot concept (a secure static analytical copy of each source is created at upload time and used for grounding), but it is not a user-restorable environment/filesystem state in the Devin/Codex sense. There is no save/restore of machine state, installed packages, or env vars, and no versioning or rollback of notebook state — deletion is terminal with no recovery. The snapshot is purely the grounding substrate, not a checkpoint users can restore. [uncertain]
cloud_local_handoff: None. NotebookLM is cloud-only (web and mobile); there is no local execution, no CLI, and no self-hosting. The only 'handoff' is external interoperability: notebooks can be mounted as data sources in the Gemini App for cross-notebook querying (early 2026). No state moves between cloud and local because there is no local runtime.
parallelism_subagent_fanout: Not a managed-agent/parallel-worker product. A single user interacts with one notebook chat at a time; there is no coordinator-of-subagents pattern, no parallel managed sessions, and no worktree fanout. Generated artifacts (Audio/Video Overview, slide deck, etc.) are produced by internal asynchronous generation jobs (e.g., audio 3-8 min, slides 60-90s), but these are not user-orchestrated parallel agents. Multiple collaborators can use a shared notebook concurrently, but each operates an independent chat. [uncertain]
trigger_surface: Sessions are initiated through the NotebookLM web app and mobile app, and (for managed) the Google Workspace surface; NotebookLM Enterprise is reached via Google Cloud / Gemini Enterprise / Agentspace. There is no public end-user API, CLI, Slack, GitHub, or cron/webhook trigger surface for NotebookLM itself. External triggering is only via the Gemini App mounting notebooks as sources.
implementation_stack: Google-proprietary, not publicly documented in detail. Model layer is the Gemini family (Gemini 2.5 Flash class) with a closed RAG retrieval pipeline over per-notebook source snapshots and a 1M-token context window (all tiers since Jan 2026). Persistence is Google cloud infrastructure; Enterprise is layered on Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise / Agentspace) with org identity via Cloud Identity or Workforce Identity Federation. Specific datastore, embedding/index, event format, and caching choices are not disclosed. [uncertain]
applicability_to_labmate: Strong template for workspace = curated corpus scope, which maps cleanly onto a Labmate workspace_id that bounds a source set rather than a filesystem path. Key transferable patterns: (1) Make the workspace a bounded, named source set whose sources are explicitly added/removed and whose retrieval (RAG) is strictly scoped to that set — Labmate can scope a workspace_id to a MongoDB-backed corpus document and constrain LangGraph retrieval to it. (2) Layer state cleanly: durable curated content (sources + saved notes) vs. resumable per-workspace chat thread — analogous to MongoDB long-term session docs (sources/notes/summaries) plus Redis Streams + LangGraph thread_id checkpointing keyed by (workspace_id, user_id) for the active resumable chat. (3) Per-user chat history scoped within a shared workspace (private chat, shared sources/artifacts) — for Labmate, key conversation threads by (workspace_id, user_id) so a Discord-shared workspace keeps shared corpus/notes but per-member private threads. (4) Citation-grounded answers with click-through to exact source passages — store source chunk offsets to support inline citations. Caveats to improve on: NotebookLM lacks cross-workspace history search, has no config/instruction-file precedence layer, and hard-deletes with no recovery — Labmate should add cross-workspace search (Mongo text/semantic index over session docs), an explicit global-vs-workspace instruction layer, and soft-delete/archival with TTL on Redis active state while retaining Mongo long-term docs.
